# Known differences from Spark 3.5 (generated by scripts/xfail_summary.py from test/xfail.toml)

Each id is an expected failure of the differential tests: the case still runs and must keep failing; a case that starts to pass makes the run fail (XPASS) until its entry is removed. `conf-rejected`, `types-ntz` and `types-interval` are the classes plan section 9 allows; the other ids are open work or documented limits.

| id | cases | files | reason | example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `types-interval` | 19041 | 32 | DuckDB has one INTERVAL type, so Spark's interval ranges are not representable (plan 9.4) | `spark_corpus__ansi__cast.sql:41  SELECT CAST("interval '3-1' year to month" AS interval year to month)` |
| `ansi-implicit-cast` | 14342 | 35 | ANSI mode changes Spark's implicit casts (AnsiTypeCoercion); the dialect keeps the non-ANSI rules | `settings__ansi_enabled.sql:2  SELECT '1' + 1, typeof('1' + 1), typeof('2' > 1), typeof(coalesce('1', 2))` |
| `types-open-c6` | 8052 | 1 | difference from Spark found by the type matrix, not yet fixed (see the case and docs/plans/spark-parity/known_differences.md) | `types__c6_function_args.sql:66  SELECT 2 % CAST(1.5 AS FLOAT)` |
| `conf-rejected` | 7174 | 58 | a setting the dialect does not emulate is rejected by SET (plan 9.1); Spark accepts it | `settings__ansi_doubleQuotedIdentifiers.sql:1  SELECT "a" FROM VALUES (1) t(a)` |
